record.title: European Ethical Charter on the use of artificial intelligence in judicial systems and their environment
record.short_title: CEPEJ European Ethical Charter on AI in Justice
record.issuing_body: European Commission for the Efficiency of Justice (CEPEJ), Council of Europe
record.summary: The first European text on ethics of AI in justice, adopted by the CEPEJ at its 31st plenary meeting. It sets five principles for the design and use of AI tools that process judicial decisions and data: respect for fundamental rights, non-discrimination, quality and security, transparency, impartiality and fairness (including external audits), and keeping users in control. Appendices give an in-depth study, a list of uses to encourage or treat with reservations, and a checklist.
record.notes: Adopted during the CEPEJ's 31st plenary meeting, held in Strasbourg on 3 and 4 December 2018; the cover of the document is dated 3 December 2018 and the Council of Europe's publication page gives 4 December 2018 as the adoption date. The Council of Europe also publishes the text in French.

judgment.status_reasoning: The CEPEJ adopted the Charter on 4 December 2018 as a set of principles to guide policy makers and justice professionals; no later amendment or withdrawal appears in the stored sources, and the Council of Europe still offers it as a publication.
judgment.scope_reasoning: AI-specific ethical principles issued by an intergovernmental body of the Council of Europe; clearly in scope, no note.

open_questions: The official PDF on rm.coe.int could not be stored (HTTP 403); the full text stored is a copy on a third-party site, so identifier and date rest partly on secondary evidence besides the Council of Europe publication page.
